node-1.label: Patient developed multiple 1- to 2-mm shiny papules on the upper limbs and body, with subsequent pruritus

node-2.label: A man in his 40s had been diagnosed with metastatic lung adenocarcinoma the previous year and received 2 courses of radiotherapy to the head and leg and 4 cycles of carboplatin, pemetrexed, and bevacizumab followed by nivolumab (3 mg/kg) every 2 weeks.

node-3.label: After 8 cycles of nivolumab over 5 months, 1- to 2-mm shiny papules appeared on the upper limbs; similar lesions spread to the rest of the body over the subsequent 3 months, followed by pruritus.

node-4.label: Physical examination showed multiple 1- to 2-mm shiny papules scattered on the upper limbs and body, with lesions on the untreated arm coalescing into plaques.

why.why: The skin biopsy after 8 cycles of nivolumab shows vacuolar interface changes with lymphohistiocytic infiltrate and melanin incontinence, and no malignant cells. Both the pathologist and laboratory physician interpret this as consistent with immune-related skin toxicity from nivolumab. Combined with the temporal relationship and pruritic papules/plaques, this strongly supports immune-related skin toxicity. Confidence is raised from 0.72 to 0.88; a small residual uncertainty remains because immunohistochemistry was not performed.

The biopsy shows no malignant cells and instead reveals an interface dermatitis typical of immune-related toxicity, which directly argues against cutaneous metastasis. The 1-2 mm shiny pruritic papules coalescing into plaques are also atypical for metastatic carcinoma. The only reason to retain any possibility is that immunohistochemistry is not available, so confidence is reduced from 0.18 to 0.05.

The biopsy confirms a non-neoplastic inflammatory process, but the specific pattern of vacuolar interface dermatitis with pigment incontinence and the clear temporal relationship with nivolumab favor immune-related skin toxicity rather than an unrelated benign papular eruption. Thus this broad alternative remains unlikely, with confidence lowered from 0.10 to 0.07.

node-8.label: Skin biopsy shows epidermal thinning, basal layer vacuolation, lymphohistiocytic infiltrate, and pigment incontinence

node-9.label: Skin biopsy shows no malignant cells or adenocarcinoma metastasis

node-10.label: Immunohistochemical staining was not performed on the skin biopsy specimen
